 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Narsing Rao Nandikonda

entities.text:
Iffcotokio General Insurance ... vs Anagandula Rajamallu ,
Enugula
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This MACMA is filed under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'MV Act') by the appellant-Insurance Company-respondent No.2 against the order and decree dated 13.12.2019 passed in M.V.O.P. No.55 of 2016 by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal cum Special Judge for trial of cases under SCs/STs (PoA) Act cum V Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Adilabad, (for short 'the Tribunal'), wherein the claimants filed the claim petition under Section 166 (1) (c) of the MV Act read with Rule 455 of the Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.7,00,000/- on account of death of the daughter of respondent Nos.1 and 2- claimants, namely, A.
Gangamani, (hereinafter referred as 'deceased'), who died in Motor Vehicle accident occurred on 09.01.2015.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are hereinafter referred as arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 09.01.2015 at about 3.45 PM, the deceased was travelling in an auto rickshaw bearing No.AP 1 X 6677 along with other passengers from Indanpalli village to Khanapur and when NNR,J they reached near Peddur Thanda village, the driver of lorry bearing No.AP 25 T 3497 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and dashed the auto in the opposite direction, due to which the deceased sustained grievous injuries on her head, chest,
ribs and other vital parts of the body.
Immediately, she was shifted to Khanapur Hospital for treatment, but died on the way to the hospital.

A case was registered by the Police, Kaddam in crime No.3 of 2015 for the offence under Section 304-A IPC against the driver of the lorry and charge sheet also filed making the driver of the lorry responsible for the accident.
4.
It was further contended by the claimants that as on the date of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 18 years and was earning Rs.200/- to Rs.300/- per day as a coolie.
Due to the death of the deceased, the claimants lost their beloved daughter and also the love and affection.
As such, the claimants claimed Rs.7,00,000/- from the respondents.
5. The respondent No.3-Owner of the crime vehicle-lorry bearing No.AP 25 T 3497 died and respondent No.4, being the wife of the respondent No.3, brought on record as his legal heir.
6. The respondent No.2 - M/s.

IFFCO TOKIO General Insurance Company Limited filed counter denying all the averments made in the claim NNR,J petition and contended that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and also denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.

1 and insurer of the auto, being the proper and necessary party was not added as parties and therefore, the petition was liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties.
It was further averred that the driver of the lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident, as such, the Insurance Company was not liable to pay compensation.
The other respondents did not choose to file counters or contest the petition.

7. Basing on the above pleadings, the learned Tribunal framed the following issues for consideration:
i) Whether the deceased A. Gangamani had died in a road accident that occurred on 09.01.2015 at about 3.45 p.m., at outskirts of Peddur Thanda village, on NH. No.61 BT road, due to the rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing No.AP 25T 3497 by respondent No.3?
ii) Whether the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP 25T 3497 is having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident?
iii) Whether the petition is bad for non-joinder of owner and insurer of the auto rickshaw bearing No. AP1X6677 as necessary party?
NNR,J iv) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and against which of the respondents?
v) To what relief?
8.
During the course of trial, the claimants examined PWs.1 and 2 and marked Exs.A1 to A8.

On behalf of the respondents, RWs.1 and 2 were examined and Ex.B1-copy of the policy was marked,
and Exs.X1 and X2 were also marked.

9. After going into the merits of the case and after considering the oral and documentary evidence placed by both the parties and the submissions of both the parties, the learned Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident occurred only due to the rash and negligent driving of lorry bearing No.
AP 25T 3497 by its driver and further held that the respondents could not able to prove that the driver was not holding valid driving licence at the time of the accident.

The learned Tribunal further held that the contention of the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that there was non-joinder of necessary parties i.e. the owner and insurer of the auto could not be accepted as it was not a valid ground and that they need not be added as parties and finally awarded an amount of Rs.6,95,400/-
as compensation to the claimants considering the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National NNR,J Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text: 2 10. Being aggrieved by the order and decree passed by the learned Tribunal, the present appeal is filed by the appellant-Insurance Company- respondent No.2 on the ground that the learned Tribunal did not consider the evidence of RWs.1 and 2, Exs.B1, X1 and X2, and also the charge sheet filed by the police against the driver of crime lorry, wherein it was stated that the driver of the lorry was not possessing any valid and effective driving licence.

It was further contended that it was the responsibility of respondent No.3- owner, who willfully entrusted the lorry to the driver knowing fully-well that the driver was not holding valid driving licence.

It was further contended that the deceased was travelling in an auto in which excess passengers were travelling as such, the accident was occurred only due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the auto as he was carrying excess passengers more than the capacity.

It was further contended that the learned Tribunal erred in taking the income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- per month without considering that the deceased was aged about 15 years and was a student and awarded the amount which was excessive and exorbitant.
11. There is no cross-appeal preferred by the claimants.
NNR,J 12.
Heard Sri K. Ajay Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant - M/s.IFFCO-TOKIO General Insurance Company Limited and Sri S. Surender Reddy, learned counsel for the respondent Nos.1 and 2-claimants.

13. Perused the record.
14.

Now, the point which arose for consideration before this Court in the present appeal is that:
Whether the appellant made any grounds to interfere with the order and decree passed by the Tribunal?
Point:
15.

Upon hearing the learned counsel for both the parties and on perusing the entire material on record, the main grievance of the appellant- Insurance Company is that the learned Tribunal did not choose to consider that there was negligence on the part of the driver of auto, who was carrying passengers more than the capacity.
Learned counsel for the appellant referred to the evidence of PW.2.
In the cross-examination, PW.2 stated that about 8 to 9 persons were travelling in the auto and that she was sitting in the back seat in between her family members.
She further stated that as she was sitting in back seat, she was not in a position to observe at whose fault the accident occurred.

Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company intending to NNR,J believe the version of PW.2 to the extent of carrying of 8 to 9 passengers, but they disbelieved her version as she was not an eye witness to the said accident.
It was the contention of the appellant that the accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the auto as he was carrying excess passengers.

In the absence of any evidence, mere carrying of excess passengers in the auto more than its capacity, cannot be a ground to consider that the accident occurred due to the negligence on M/S Iffcotokio General Insurance ... vs Anagandula Rajamallu , Enugula ... on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41268952/
3 the part of the auto driver.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The charge sheet filed by the police would clearly reveal that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry at whose negligence the said accident occurred.

16. Besides that, the other ground which the learned counsel for the appellant has pressed was that the learned Tribunal did not choose to consider the aspect of non-possessing of driving licence by the driver of the crime lorry.

In support of his contention, learned counsel for the appellant relied upon the evidence of RWs.1 and 2, wherein RWs.1 and 2 specifically stated that the Police charge sheeted the driver of the lorry under Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act as the driver of the crime vehicle was not having valid driving licence at the time of the accident.

In his evidence,
RW.2-Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector, Nizamabad, had specifically stated that as per their NNR,J records, it was found that the driver of the lorry i.e. Shaik Lal Mohammed was not issued any sort of driving licence from their RTO.

He also filed a memo under Ex.X2 which clearly would show that there was no driving licence possessed by the driver of the crime vehicle, which the learned Tribunal has missed sight and did not accept the version of RW.2 on the ground that owner of the crime vehicle was not being summoned nor he was examined before the Court.

As such, the learned Tribunal did not believe the version of the appellant-Insurance Company, which appears to be an error committed by the learned Tribunal though the appellant-Insurance Company had discharged their burden by examining the RTO official to show that the driver was not having valid driving licence.

17. The other ground raised by the appellant-Insurance Company was that the learned Tribunal did not consider the aspect of non-joinder of the necessary parties i.e. owner and insurer of the auto, but there were no findings given by the learned Tribunal in respect of the said issue of non-joinder of the Owner and Insurer of the auto rickshaw, which was fatal to the case of the appellant.

18. In respect of quantum of compensation, the learned Tribunal had rightly taken into consideration the income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- per NNR,J month by placing reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited [2011 (6) ALD 75 (SC)] and addition of future prospects by relying the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company v. Pranay Sethi and Others and by adopting proper multiplier, and also the amounts under conventional heads i.e. funeral expenses, loss of estate, and awarded just, fair and reasonable amount of Rs.6,95,400/- with interest at 7.5% per annum.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Company v. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the said findings and the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal.

19. Further, this Court is of the opinion that the learned Tribunal though initially imposed the burden of payment of compensation on the appellant-Insurance Company, it ought to have considered the aspect of pay and recovery as the Insurance Company had placed before the learned Tribunal the evidence of RWs.1 and 2, which substantially proved that the there was no licence being possessed by the driver of the crime vehicle i.e. lorry bearing No.AP 25T 3497 and the owner of the lorry did not place evidence to show that he has no knowledge about the non-possessing of the licence by the driver of the said lorry.

Hence, in the said circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that the order and decree passed by the learned Tribunal can be interfered only to the extent of permitting the appellant-Insurance Company to pay the compensation initially and seek recovery of the same from the owner of the crime lorry under the same decree.
The point is answered accordingly.

21. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent of directing the appellant-Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount as awarded by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal cum Special Judge for trial of cases under SCs/STs (PoA) Act cum V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Adilabad vide order dated 13.12.2019 in M.V.O.P. No.55 of 2016 initially and then recover the same from the owner of the crime vehicle.
